newsitem.title: USA: U.S. renews warning against Serbian crackdown.
newsitem.headline: U.S. renews warning against Serbian crackdown.

text.p: The United States renewed a warning on Monday against any crackdown on political opponents of President Slobodan Milosevic, who demanded their victory in local elections be restored.

"We've warned the Serbian government repeatedly that a crackdown against the protesters will have serious consequences and lead to Serbia's further isolation from the international community," acting State Department spokesman Glyn Davies said.
He heaped scorn on what he called "rent-a-crowd" counter-demonstrations organised by the ruling party.
"We urge the authorities to focus on resolving the political crisis sparked by the annulment of the Nov. 17 opposition victories in the municipal elections," Davies said.
"They should do that rather than encourage actions that could produce further confrontation in the street," he said.

In Belgrade, up to 40,000 students marched for the 35th day on Sunday, while some 80,000 opposition supporters packed a central square sending a stark message to the authorities -- bad weather, random arrests or threats by pro-Milosevic demonstrations will not silence their demand for democracy.
